transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in today. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you or what brings you here?

Hi, doctor. Thanks for, uh, taking the time to see me. I really appreciate it, and I hope I'm not wasting your time or anything. 

I guess I came in because... well, I recently had to move into this new room, and it's kind of busted-up. I mean, it's not the worst, I shouldn't complain, but I've been staying up super late trying to fix leaks and get the heat working. And... well, I'm a little embarrassed to admit it, but I've been dragging myself into work late because of it. 

I do construction, and lately I'm just messing up stuff I normally handle no problem. I've even been snapping at the other guys, which really isn't like me. I don't want you to think I'm a hothead or a bad worker, it's just... it's been a lot. 

Is that... is that the kind of stuff you wanted to know? I just want to make sure I'm answering your question right.
Have you noticed that you’re not enjoying things that you usually like to do, like hobbies or spending time with friends?

Oh, um, no, I don't think so. I still like hanging out with my buddies and watching the game and stuff. I mean, I haven't had as much time for it lately because I've been trying to fix up the room every night, but when I do get a chance to see them, I still enjoy it just fine. 

I definitely try to keep up with my friends. I don't want you to think I'm just shutting everyone out or giving up on things, because I'm really not. I hope that's a good sign? Like, I still want to do all my normal stuff, it's just the tiredness getting in the way. Does that help answer your question? I can try to explain it better if you need me to.
Have you found yourself feeling down or depressed most of the day, even when you're not tired or stressed about fixing the room?

No, no, I wouldn't say I'm depressed. I mean, sure, I get a little bummed out when I'm wrestling with a pipe at two in the morning, but... during the day? No, I'm okay. Like, I don't walk around feeling sad all the time or anything like that. 

I really try to keep a positive attitude, you know? I'm just worn out from the move and the room. If I could just get a good night's sleep, I think I'd be completely back to normal. I hope it doesn't sound like I'm, you know, whining about it too much. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture. I'm not a depressed kind of guy, just... just a little overwhelmed right now, I guess. Is that okay?

latest_inference.note: The patient denied feeling down or depressed most of the day, and reports that their issues are related to stress and fatigue from moving and fixing the room rather than a loss of interest or pleasure in activities. This rules out most depressive disorders (F32.0-F32.9, F33.0-F33.9). The presentation is more consistent with adjustment disorder with mixed anxiety and depressed mood (F43.22).

inference_history.note: Presenting concerns include sleep disruption, functional impairment at work, and irritability following a stressful life event (moving into a new, substandard living situation). These symptoms could indicate an adjustment disorder with depressed mood (F43.22) or a major depressive episode (various F32 codes) especially if symptoms are severe or persistent. There is insufficient information at this stage to differentiate between these possibilities.
